messages:
olivia-cs: customer reports intermittent 403 on /v1/embeddings even though same API key works for chat generation. says it started after we rolled their edge proxy change yesterday.

marta-support: do we have request examples? headers?

olivia-cs: pasted curl they ran (sanitized token):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-XXXXX, sk-pool-YYYYY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

olivia-cs: they said they multiplex tokens in a single header for routing to different backends. sometimes returns 200 for chat endpoints but embeddings returns 403. :thinking_face:

henry-eng-platform: whoa the Authorization header contains two tokens separated by a comma. we never supported comma-separated bearer lists on the API side; we only parse the first Bearer token and treat it as the credential. if the first token is a pool token without embeddings scope, that explains 403.

simon-ops: why would chat succeed then?

henry-eng-platform: chat route is hitting a fallback service that accepts pool tokens for generation due to legacy routing rules. embeddings route is stricter and enforces exact scope claims. mismatch manifests as intermittent failures depending which token is first.

marta-support: customer says it used to work before the proxy change. could the proxy be reordering or concatenating headers?

simon-ops: checked edge-proxy logs — it applies header stitching when clients attach multiple keys and rewrites to a single Authorization header using a comma-separated list. That was a recent convenience change for the vendor. it collapsed multiple auth headers into one.

henry-eng-platform: repro steps I ran locally:
```
# send two headers separately -> server receives first only
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ok' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-no-embeds' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{}'
# server log shows: Authorization: Bearer sk-ok

# send single header with comma-> server receives entire string but our parser extracts token before first comma
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-no-embeds, sk-ok" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{}'
# server sees first token sk-no-embeds -> 403
```

olivia-cs: customer can reproduce reliably with their proxy. they want either a fix on our side or a config change for them.

henry-eng-platform: short-term mitigation ideas:
- ask customer to stop multiplexing and send a single valid token (document recommended)
- accept fallback if second token has broader scopes? risky.

edge-proxy-bot: NOTE: vendor proxy change rolled 2026-03-10 03:12Z that collapses duplicate headers into a single header with comma-separated values.

simon-ops: long term we could accept comma-separated Bearer lists and try tokens sequentially until one authorizes the requested scope. that should preserve backward compatibility. but need to think about logging/audit implications.

henry-eng-platform: agree. implementation notes: parse Authorization value for multiple comma/semicolon separated tokens, trim whitespace, attempt validate_token for each in order. return first success. add server-side metric `auth.multiple_token_attempts` and log anonymized token ids for debugging.

marta-support: any security concerns?

henry-eng-platform: small: makes our auth path do extra lookups per request in worst case. also consider rate-limit/backoff if pools are used to avoid enumeration attacks. we can gate for `Content-Type: application/json` endpoints first.

olivia-cs: customer ok with a documented config change to their proxy for now. asked if we can ship a soft-fix this week.

simon-ops: i'll open an eng-infra ticket and mark P2: rapid patch to auth parser. will include test cases: single token, comma-separated, semicolon, multiple Authorization headers.

henry-eng-platform: I'll draft the PR and add a feature flag `auth.allow_multi_bearer` default false. once validated we'll enable in prod and notify customers.

olivia-cs: thanks team — i'll reply to customer with repro explanation + short-term proxy workaround: configure proxy to forward only one Authorization header (the intended token) or stop combining headers into a CSV. i'll link the ticket once created. :white_check_mark:
